guide.q.supported_payment_providers: Which payment companies can I use?
guide.a.supported_payment_providers:
Stripe, Square, and SumUp. Choose one in Settings and enter your key. You can switch between them at any time.

SumUp works only with some currencies (mostly European ones, plus GBP, USD, and BRL). If your site's currency is not on their list, the Settings page refuses the details and asks you to pick a different company.
guide.q.recommended_payment_provider: Which payment company do you recommend?
guide.a.recommended_payment_provider:
Stripe. It is the quickest to set up — you paste in one key and everything else is done for you. SumUp is nearly as quick, but it works only with some currencies. Square asks you to create a developer app, find your location ID, and add a webhook by hand.

All three work well once set up.
guide.q.paid_ticket_booking_flow: What happens when someone books a paid ticket?
guide.a.paid_ticket_booking_flow:
They fill in the booking form, then go to your payment company's own payment page. When their payment goes through, their place is saved and they get their ticket.

Their place is not held while they are paying. See Why don't we hold places during checkout? below for the reason.
guide.q.listing_sells_out_while_paying: What if the listing sells out while someone is paying?
guide.a.listing_sells_out_while_paying:
If someone finishes paying but the listing has sold out in the meantime, they get their money back straight away. They see a message saying the listing is full and their payment has been returned.

This is rare, but it can happen. It is the trade-off described in the question above.
guide.a.how_refunds_work: See the Refunds section below for everything: money back given by the system, refunds you send yourself, and refunding everyone at once.
guide.q.find_stripe_secret_key: How do I find my Stripe secret key?
guide.a.find_stripe_secret_key:
Your key is a long password that lets this site take payments through your Stripe account. To find it:

  1. Log in to your Stripe account
  2. Click Developers in the menu
  3. Select API keys from the sidebar
  4. Under Standard keys, find the Secret key row and click Reveal
  5. Copy the key. It starts with sk_live_ for real payments, or sk_test_ for trying things out
  6. Paste it into the Stripe Secret Key field on the Settings page

Tip: try a sk_test_ key first. Test mode lets you make bookings without any real money moving.
guide.q.stripe_webhook_setup: Do I need to set up a Stripe webhook myself?
guide.a.stripe_webhook_setup:
No. A webhook is a message Stripe sends this site when a payment completes. When you save your Stripe key in Settings, this site sets that message up inside your Stripe account for you.

To check it works, click the Test Connection button that appears after you save your key.
guide.q.create_square_application: How do I create a Square application?
guide.a.create_square_application:
Before you can take payments with Square, you create an app in your Square account. This is a one-off job that gives you the details this site needs.

  1. Go to the Square apps page and sign in with your Square account
  2. Click the + button to make a new app
  3. Give it a name (your organisation's name is fine) and click Save

Once it exists, your access token and location ID are on its pages — see the next two questions.
guide.q.find_square_access_token: How do I find my Square access token?
guide.a.find_square_access_token:
1. Log in to the Square apps page
  2. Select your app
  3. Open the Credentials page
  4. Copy the Access token. Use the Sandbox one for trying things out, and the Production one for real payments
  5. Paste it into the Square Access Token field on the Settings page
guide.q.find_square_location_id: How do I find my Square location ID?
guide.a.find_square_location_id:
1. Log in to the Square apps page and select your app
  2. Open the Locations page in the sidebar
  3. Copy the Location ID for the place you take payments for

You can also find it in the main Square Dashboard, under Account & Settings → Business information → Locations.
guide.q.setup_square_webhook: How do I set up the Square webhook?
guide.a.setup_square_webhook:
A webhook is a message Square sends this site when a payment completes. Unlike Stripe, Square asks you to set this up by hand. After saving your Square access token and location ID:

  1. Go to the Square apps page and select your app
  2. Open Webhooks in the sidebar
  3. Click Add Subscription
  4. Set the Notification URL to the webhook address shown on your Settings page
  5. Tick the payment.updated event
  6. Save, then copy the Signature Key Square shows you
  7. Paste the signature key into the webhook field on your Settings page

Bookings are not confirmed until this is done, because the webhook is how Square tells this site a payment finished.
guide.q.square_link_ends: How long can someone pay with a Square payment link?
guide.a.square_link_ends: Square ends an unpaid payment link 180 days after it is made. A link also ends once it has been paid. After that, the buyer cannot pay with it and must book again.
guide.q.stripe_test_vs_live_keys: What is the difference between Stripe test and live keys?
guide.a.stripe_test_vs_live_keys:
Stripe gives you two separate modes, each with its own keys:

  • Test keys (sk_test_) — a practice mode. No real money moves. You can use Stripe's made-up test card numbers to try successful and failed payments. Test bookings do not appear in your real Stripe account.
  • Live keys (sk_live_) — the real thing. Real cards are charged and real money arrives in your account.

This site can tell which one you are using from the start of the key, and shows it on the Settings page. Only keys starting with sk_test_ or sk_live_ are accepted.
guide.q.test_or_live_credentials: Should I use test or live details?
guide.a.test_or_live_credentials:
Start with test details and make one booking all the way through. Then switch to live details when you are ready for real money.

  • Stripe: use a key starting with sk_test_. The Settings page shows a Test mode badge so you always know where you are.
  • Square: use your Sandbox access token and location, and tick the Sandbox mode box on the Settings page. Untick it when you go live.
  • SumUp: create a sandbox merchant account, then use its API key and merchant code — see How do I set up SumUp? below for where to find both. Swap to your real account's key and merchant code to go live.

When you are ready, put your live details into Settings.
guide.q.automatic_refunds: When does the system give money back by itself?
guide.a.automatic_refunds:
A place only counts as taken once payment finishes — nothing is held during checkout (see Why don't we hold places during checkout? above). Because of that, a finished payment can sometimes arrive after the booking stopped being possible. When that happens, the money goes back to the buyer automatically.

This happens when, by the time the payment completes:

  • the listing has sold out — someone else took the last place first, so the slower buyer gets their money back and a message saying the listing is full;
  • the price changed — you edited the price while they were paying, so the amount they paid no longer matches;
  • the listing was closed or switched off while they were paying.

For multi-listing bookings it is all-or-nothing: if any one listing fails, the whole payment goes back — not just the part for that listing.
guide.q.refund_individual_attendee: How do I refund one attendee?
guide.a.refund_individual_attendee:
Open the listing's attendee list, find the attendee, and click Refund. You will see a page showing their name, email, quantity, and what they paid. Type the attendee's name to confirm.

The money goes back through your payment company (Stripe, Square, or SumUp). It is always the whole amount — you cannot send back part of it.
guide.q.refund_all_attendees: How do I refund all attendees for a listing?
guide.a.refund_all_attendees:
On the listing page, click Refund All in the bar at the top. Type the listing's name to confirm. Everyone with a recorded payment is refunded one by one.

If some refunds fail (for example a payment was already refunded in your payment company's own dashboard), you see how many worked and how many did not.
guide.q.partial_refunds: Can I refund part of a payment?
guide.a.partial_refunds: No. This site always sends back the full amount. If you need to send back only part of it, do it in your payment company's own dashboard (Stripe, Square, or SumUp).
guide.q.attendee_after_refund: What happens to the attendee after a refund?
guide.a.attendee_after_refund:
The attendee stays on the list. A refund only clears their payment record — it does not remove them. If you want them gone too, delete them separately after refunding.

Refunds work per listing. If the attendee is booked on several listings, refunding one does not touch the others.
guide.q.refund_free_listing: Can I refund an attendee who booked a free listing?
guide.a.refund_free_listing: No. The Refund button appears only for attendees who paid something. A free booking has no payment to return.
guide.a.refund_fails:
The most common reason is that the payment was already refunded in your payment company's own dashboard. You see a message like "Refund failed. The payment may have already been refunded."

Refunds also fail if your payment company is no longer set up — there is nowhere to send the money back through.
guide.q.refund_same_attendee_twice: Can I refund the same attendee twice?
guide.a.refund_same_attendee_twice: No. After a successful refund the payment record is cleared, so the Refund button disappears. If the payment was already refunded in your payment company's dashboard, the company refuses the second try and you see a failure message.
guide.a.what_is_the_money_ledger:
Money shows every money change on your site. Each row says what happened and when.

Checkout and refund records cannot be changed or deleted. Later corrections sit beside the original records. This keeps the full history clear.

Simple view explains each change in plain words. Detailed view shows where the money moved. Select a linked name to see its running total. Each attendee has their own Money page too.
guide.q.ledger_accounts_explained: What do the names in Detailed view mean?
guide.a.ledger_accounts_explained:
Most names are a listing, attendee, or option. Select a linked name to see its Money.

Three names always mean the same thing:

  • Card / bank — money received from, or returned to, a customer.
  • Booking fees — booking fee income added to ticket prices.
  • Corrections — changes that keep the other totals correct.
guide.q.ledger_entry_kinds: What do the different money changes mean?
guide.a.ledger_entry_kinds:
Each change has a short label:

  • Booking made — ticket income recorded when someone books.
  • Payment received — a deposit or full payment was received.
  • Booking fee — booking fee income was added.
  • Price change — a discount or extra charge changed the price.
  • Refund — money was returned. The related booking, fee, and price changes were also removed from the totals.
  • Service event cost — a servicing job's cost was recorded for a listing.
  • Correction — an earlier total was corrected.
  • Change reversed — an admin action exactly cancelled an earlier change.
guide.q.ledger_manual_entries: How do I record a waived amount or another money change?
guide.a.ledger_manual_entries:
Open Money for an attendee, listing, or option. Select Add money change. Choose what happened and enter the amount.

The new change updates the running total without changing earlier records. The option appears only where you can add a money change.
guide.a.how_daily_listings_work: Daily listings let attendees pick a date when they book. You set which days of the week are open (for example Monday to Friday), how soon a date can be booked, and how far ahead dates are shown. The people limit applies to each date on its own.
guide.a.what_are_bookable_days: These are the days of the week your daily listing runs on. If you only tick Monday and Wednesday, those are the only days that appear in the date picker. Weekends and unticked days are skipped.
guide.a.what_are_holidays: Holidays are date ranges when no daily listings can be booked — Christmas week, for example. Add them on the Holidays page. Any dates inside a holiday are removed from the booking calendar for every daily listing.
guide.q.why_don_t_we_hold_places_during: Why don't we hold places during checkout?
guide.a.why_don_t_we_hold_places_during:
When someone clicks "Buy", their place is not kept while they pay. A place only counts as taken once the payment goes through. That might sound backwards, so here is why.

Imagine we did keep places during payment. Someone could write a small program that opens the payment page over and over, grabbing every place, without ever paying. Real visitors would see "sold out" even though nobody had actually bought anything. When the holds ran out, the program could grab them all again. This is how ticket scalpers cause trouble on bigger sites.

Because places only count once payment is finished, the only way to hold a place is to actually pay for it. Real money has to change hands — so the trick does not work, and real visitors get a fair chance at the tickets.

The trade-off: very rarely, two people finish paying for the last place at almost the same moment. The first payment to arrive wins; the second person gets their money back automatically. See the next question.
guide.q.is_the_booking_fee_refunded_too: Is the booking fee refunded too?
guide.a.is_the_booking_fee_refunded_too:
Yes. A refund sends back the whole amount taken from the attendee, including any booking fee added at checkout.

Your payment company's own charge is separate. Stripe and Square each decide for themselves whether to return their slice on a refund, so check with them.
guide.q.how_do_i_set_up_sumup: How do I set up SumUp?
guide.a.how_do_i_set_up_sumup:
You need two values, and both must come from the same SumUp account:

  1. API Key — from your SumUp account. The page is tucked away: go to Profile → Settings → For Developers → Toolkit → API Keys, or use this direct link: me.sumup.com/en-gb/settings/api-keys. That page shows a Public API key near the top — that is not the one you need. In the API Keys section below it, click Create API key, give it a name, and copy the new private key. It is shown only once.
  2. Merchant Code — a short code, usually starting with M, shown in your SumUp account under your profile or account settings.

Paste both into the SumUp section on the Settings page and save. Then click Test Connection. The test checks that the key and the merchant code belong to the same account. If they do not — for example a sandbox key with a live merchant code — it reports a 401 Unauthorized error. If you see that, copy the key again in full and check the merchant code comes from the same SumUp account.

There is nothing else to set up: SumUp's payment page and webhook are handled for you.

SumUp works only with some currencies. If your site's currency is not one of them, saving is blocked and you are asked to choose a different company.
